text.text: Vibeprint: how does an iPad sketch survive a page reload?
New engineers · Direct LAN canvas sync only: iPad browser, local vibeprint daemon, and .vibeprint/canvas.json on disk.

Token-gated LAN
server; owns live
canvas

Canvas shapes on
disk in the repo

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient,
response included; dashed = async; dotted = local command/I/O. Flow type is also written on each arrow.

The daemon acks an op once it is
applied in memory. The save runs on
an 800ms timer after the last edit, so
a daemon crash before the timer fires
loses the latest edits.

If the socket drops, the browser
retries with backoff (500ms up to
10s). On the new snapshot it replays
its unacked ops, but those live only in
page memory, so a full reload drops
them.

If canvas.json won't parse or isn't a
Vibeprint canvas, loading throws and
says to restore it from git. A single
unreadable shape is skipped and
logged.
Outside this view: MCP agent tools, AI map redraws and the Fly relay path; Marks/chat persistence, image assets and git checkpoints.
